notes: Bar/B-style eye-shape calls are treated as weaker standalone sorting markers.
Curly wings are treated as the most reliable dominant balancer marker.
Stubble is a useful balancer marker but less stable than Curly in routine sorting.
Tubby is down-weighted because TM6B/Tb reversion is a known high-frequency risk.

payload.effect: cut wing margin with missing margin tissue
rough eyes with missing R7 photoreceptors
abnormal wing posture or flight from tendon defects
reduced drop-shaped eyes with locomotor defects
flightless wings from defective tendon attachment
glazed rough eyes with abnormal pigmentation

notes: Modeled as a third-chromosome dominant marker balancer shorthand.
Uses the cheat-sheet visible-marker set for the common second-chromosome balancer.
Bare FM7 is kept conservative; specific FM7 variants carry the fuller cheat-sheet marker sets.
Preserves the FM7c-specific sn marker instead of collapsing to generic FM7.
Treated as the same visible-marker set as MKRS for phenotype summaries.
Bare TM3 follows the conservative BDSC core visible-marker set.
Explicit Sb[1] and Ser[1] in genotype strings are resolved separately rather than implied by TM3.
Uses the stripped-down TM6C visible core from the cheat sheet rather than the fuller TM6B shorthand.
mini-white eye pigmentation is dosage-sensitive and varies with insertion context.
